sanskrit: evaṃ mamāpi putrasya putraḥ pitaram anvagāt duryodhanaṃ mahābāho lakṣmaṇaḥ paravīrahā
english: So too, O mighty-armed one, the son of my son followed his father: Lakṣmaṇa, slayer of enemy heroes, went after Duryodhana.

sanskrit: vindānuvindāv āvantyau patitau paśya mādhava himānte puṣpitau śālau marutā galitāv iva
english: Behold, O Mādhava, Vinda and Anuvinda, the two princes of Avanti, fallen — like a pair of sāla trees in bloom at winter's end, brought down by the wind.

sanskrit: kāñcanāṅgadavarmāṇau bāṇakhaḍgadhanurdharau ṛṣabhapratirūpākṣau śayānau vimalasrajau
english: Armored, with golden armlets, bearers of arrow, sword, and bow, their eyes like a bull's, they lie there still, their garlands yet unstained.

sanskrit: avadhyāḥ pāṇḍavāḥ kṛṣṇa sarva eva tvayā saha ye muktā droṇabhīṣmābhyāṃ karṇād vaikartanāt kṛpāt
english: Unslayable were the Pāṇḍavas, O Kṛṣṇa, every one of them, with you beside them — they who escaped Droṇa and Bhīṣma, Karṇa son of the Sun, and Kṛpa,

sanskrit: duryodhanād droṇasutāt saindhavāc ca mahārathāt somadattād vikarṇāc ca śūrāc ca kṛtavarmaṇaḥ ye hanyuḥ śastravegena devān api nararṣabhāḥ
english: Duryodhana, the son of Droṇa, the lord of Sindhu, that great chariot-warrior, Somadatta, Vikarṇa, and the valiant Kṛtavarman — those bulls among men who by the force of their weapons could have struck down even the gods.

sanskrit: ta ime nihatāḥ saṃkhye paśya kālasya paryayam nātibhāro 'sti daivasya dhruvaṃ mādhava kaś cana yad ime nihatāḥ śūrāḥ kṣatriyaiḥ kṣatriyarṣabhāḥ
english: Yet here they lie, slain in battle — behold the turning of Time. Surely, O Mādhava, no burden is too heavy for fate, since these heroes, these bulls among the Kṣatriyas, have been slain by Kṣatriyas.

sanskrit: tadaiva nihatāḥ kṛṣṇa mama putrās tarasvinaḥ yadaivākṛtakāmas tvam upaplavyaṃ gataḥ punaḥ
english: My swift and valiant sons were as good as slain, O Kṛṣṇa, on that very day when you returned to Upaplavya with your purpose unachieved.

sanskrit: śaṃtanoś caiva putreṇa prājñena vidureṇa ca tadaivoktāsmi mā snehaṃ kuruṣvātmasuteṣv iti
english: On that day Śantanu's son and wise Vidura both told me: 'Do not set your love upon your own sons.'

sanskrit: tayor na darśanaṃ tāta mithyā bhavitum arhati acireṇaiva me putrā bhasmībhūtā janārdana
english: Their foresight, my child, could not prove false: in but a little while my sons have been reduced to ashes, O Janārdana.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktvā nyapatad bhūmau gāndhārī śokakarśitā duḥkhopahatavijñānā dhairyam utsṛjya bhārata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus, Gāndhārī, wasted by grief, her senses shattered by sorrow, abandoned her composure and fell to the ground, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tataḥ kopaparītāṅgī putraśokapariplutā jagāma śauriṃ doṣeṇa gāndhārī vyathitendriyā
english: Then Gāndhārī, her whole body seized by anger, drowned in grief for her sons, her senses tormented, turned in reproach upon the scion of the Śūras.

sanskrit: gāndhāry uvāca pāṇḍavā dhārtarāṣṭrāś ca drugdhāḥ kṛṣṇa parasparam upekṣitā vinaśyantas tvayā kasmāj janārdana
english: Gāndhārī said: The Pāṇḍavas and the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra wronged one another, O Kṛṣṇa. Why then, O Janārdana, did you stand by and let them destroy themselves?

sanskrit: śaktena bahubhṛtyena vipule tiṣṭhatā bale ubhayatra samarthena śrutavākyena caiva ha
english: You were able, with many retainers, standing amid a vast host, with power over both sides, and your word was heeded —

sanskrit: icchatopekṣito nāśaḥ kurūṇāṃ madhusūdana yasmāt tvayā mahābāho phalaṃ tasmād avāpnuhi
english: yet the ruin of the Kurus you let pass by, willingly, O slayer of Madhu. Since you did so, O mighty-armed one, reap now its fruit.

sanskrit: patiśuśrūṣayā yan me tapaḥ kiṃ cid upārjitam tena tvāṃ duravāpātmañ śapsye cakragadādhara
english: By whatever austerity I have gathered through devotion to my husband, by that, O you whose self is so hard to win, I will curse you, O bearer of discus and mace.

sanskrit: yasmāt parasparaṃ ghnanto jñātayaḥ kurupāṇḍavāḥ upekṣitās te govinda tasmāj jñātīn vadhiṣyasi
english: Because you stood by, O Govinda, while the kinsmen — Kurus and Pāṇḍavas alike — slew one another, you yourself shall slay your kinsmen.

sanskrit: tvam apy upasthite varṣe ṣaṭtriṃśe madhusūdana hatajñātir hatāmātyo hataputro vanecaraḥ kutsitenābhyupāyena nidhanaṃ samavāpsyasi
english: You too, O slayer of Madhu, when the thirty-sixth year arrives — your kinsmen slain, your counselors slain, your sons slain — wandering in the forest, shall meet your death by a contemptible means.

sanskrit: tavāpy evaṃ hatasutā nihatajñātibāndhavāḥ striyaḥ paripatiṣyanti yathaitā bharatastriyaḥ
english: And your women too, their sons slain, their kinsmen and friends struck down, shall fall about in just this way, as these women of the Bharatas do now.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tac chrutvā vacanaṃ ghoraṃ vāsudevo mahāmanāḥ uvāca devīṃ gāndhārīm īṣad abhyutsmayann iva
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing those dreadful words, the great-minded Vāsudeva spoke to the lady Gāndhārī, smiling faintly:

sanskrit: saṃhartā vṛṣṇicakrasya nānyo mad vidyate śubhe jāne 'ham etad apy evaṃ cīrṇaṃ carasi kṣatriye
english: None other than I is the destroyer of the host of the Vṛṣṇis, O gracious lady. This I already know; yet you do but accomplish what is fated, O Kṣatriya woman.

sanskrit: avadhyās te narair anyair api vā devadānavaiḥ parasparakṛtaṃ nāśam ataḥ prāpsyanti yādavāḥ
english: They cannot be slain by any other men, nor by gods nor demons; therefore the Yādavas shall meet a ruin wrought by their own hands upon one another.

sanskrit: ity uktavati dāśārhe pāṇḍavās trastacetasaḥ babhūvur bhṛśasaṃvignā nirāśāś cāpi jīvite
english: When the lord of the Dāśārhas had spoken thus, the Pāṇḍavas grew sick at heart, deeply shaken, and despaired even of life.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha gāndhāri mā ca śoke manaḥ kṛthāḥ tavaiva hy aparādhena kuravo nidhanaṃ gatāḥ
english: Vāsudeva said: Rise, rise up, Gāndhārī, and do not set your mind on grief. For it was through your own fault that the Kurus went to their destruction.

sanskrit: yā tvaṃ putraṃ durātmānam īrṣum atyantamāninam duryodhanaṃ puraskṛtya duṣkṛtaṃ sādhu manyase
english: You who, setting your evil-souled, envious, overweening son Duryodhana before all, deemed wrongdoing to be right —

sanskrit: niṣṭhuraṃ vairaparuṣaṃ vṛddhānāṃ śāsanātigam katham ātmakṛtaṃ doṣaṃ mayy ādhātum ihecchasi
english: he who was cruel, harsh in his enmity, defiant of the counsel of his elders — how can you wish to lay upon me the fault of your own making?

sanskrit: mṛtaṃ vā yadi vā naṣṭaṃ yo 'tītam anuśocati duḥkhena labhate duḥkhaṃ dvāv anarthau prapadyate
english: Whoever grieves over what is past — the dead or the lost — gains but sorrow through sorrow, and falls into a twofold misfortune.

sanskrit: taporthīyaṃ brāhmaṇī dhatta garbhaṃ; gaur voḍhāraṃ dhāvitāraṃ turaṃgī śūdrā dāsaṃ paśupālaṃ tu vaiśyā; vadhārthīyaṃ tvadvidhā rājaputrī
english: A Brāhmaṇa woman bears her child for austerity, a cow her calf to bear burdens, a mare hers to run, a Śūdra woman bears a servant and a Vaiśya woman a herdsman — but a king's daughter such as you bears her son for slaughter.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tac chrutvā vāsudevasya punaruktaṃ vaco 'priyam tūṣṇīṃ babhūva gāndhārī śokavyākulalocanā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing again these unwelcome words of Vāsudeva, Gāndhārī fell silent, her eyes troubled with grief.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭras tu rājarṣir nigṛhyābuddhijaṃ tamaḥ paryapṛcchata dharmātmā dharmarājaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram
english: But Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the royal sage, righteous of soul, having restrained the darkness born of unwisdom, questioned Yudhiṣṭhira, the king of righteousness:

sanskrit: jīvatāṃ parimāṇajñaḥ sainyānām asi pāṇḍava hatānāṃ yadi jānīṣe parimāṇaṃ vadasva me
english: You know the count of the living among the armies, O Pāṇḍava. If you know the count of the slain as well, tell it to me.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca daśāyutānām ayutaṃ sahasrāṇi ca viṃśatiḥ koṭyaḥ ṣaṣṭiś ca ṣaṭ caiva ye 'smin rājamṛdhe hatāḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: One billion six hundred and sixty million and twenty thousand are they who have been slain in this battle of kings.

sanskrit: alakṣyāṇāṃ tu vīrāṇāṃ sahasrāṇi caturdaśa daśa cānyāni rājendra śataṃ ṣaṣṭiś ca pañca ca
english: And of the heroes whose fate is unknown, there are twenty-four thousand, O lord of kings, and one hundred and sixty-five besides.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca yudhiṣṭhira gatiṃ kāṃ te gatāḥ puruṣasattamāḥ ācakṣva me mahābāho sarvajño hy asi me mataḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Yudhiṣṭhira, to what state have those best of men gone? Tell me, O mighty-armed one, for I hold you to be all-knowing.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca yair hutāni śarīrāṇi hṛṣṭaiḥ paramasaṃyuge devarājasamāṃl lokān gatās te satyavikramāḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Those who, exulting, offered up their bodies in that supreme conflict — those of true valor have gone to worlds equal to the realm of the king of the gods.

sanskrit: ye tv ahṛṣṭena manasā martavyam iti bhārata yudhyamānā hatāḥ saṃkhye te gandharvaiḥ samāgatāḥ
english: But those who fought thinking gloomily, 'I must die,' O Bhārata, and so were slain in battle — they have joined the company of the Gandharvas.

sanskrit: ye tu saṃgrāmabhūmiṣṭhā yācamānāḥ parāṅmukhāḥ śastreṇa nidhanaṃ prāptā gatās te guhyakān prati
english: Those who, standing on the field of battle, met their death by the weapon while begging or turning their backs in flight — they have gone among the Guhyakas.

sanskrit: pīḍyamānāḥ parair ye tu hīyamānā nirāyudhāḥ hrīniṣedhā mahātmānaḥ parān abhimukhā raṇe
english: Those great souls who, hard pressed by the foe, deserted and weaponless, yet restrained by shame, faced their enemies in the fray —

sanskrit: chidyamānāḥ śitaiḥ śastraiḥ kṣatradharmaparāyaṇāḥ gatās te brahmasadanaṃ hatā vīrāḥ suvarcasaḥ
english: those heroes of bright splendor, hewn by sharp weapons, devoted to the law of the warrior, when slain have gone to the abode of Brahmā.

sanskrit: ye tatra nihatā rājann antar āyodhanaṃ prati yathā kathaṃ cit te rājan saṃprāptā uttarān kurūn
english: Those who were slain there, O king, somewhere in the midst of the battle — they, O king, have attained the Northern Kurus.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca kena jñānabalenaivaṃ putra paśyasi siddhavat tan me vada mahābāho śrotavyaṃ yadi vai mayā
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: By what power of knowledge, my son, do you see all this as one perfected? Tell me, O mighty-armed one, if it may be heard by me.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca nideśād bhavataḥ pūrvaṃ vane vicaratā mayā tīrthayātrāprasaṅgena saṃprāpto 'yam anugrahaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Long ago, at your command, as I wandered through the forest on a pilgrimage to the sacred fords, this grace was won by me.

sanskrit: devarṣir lomaśo dṛṣṭas tataḥ prāpto 'smy anusmṛtim divyaṃ cakṣur api prāptaṃ jñānayogena vai purā
english: There I beheld the divine sage Lomaśa, and through him I gained the power of recollection; and the divine eye too I obtained long ago through the discipline of knowledge.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca ye 'trānāthā janasyāsya sanāthā ye ca bhārata kaccit teṣāṃ śarīrāṇi dhakṣyanti vidhipūrvakam
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Among these people, O Bhārata, are those who have kinsmen and those who have none. Will their bodies be burned according to rite?

sanskrit: na yeṣāṃ santi kartāro na ca ye 'trāhitāgnayaḥ vayaṃ ca kasya kuryāmo bahutvāt tāta karmaṇaḥ
english: For those who have none to perform the rites, and those who tended no sacred fire — for whom among such a multitude shall we perform them, my son, so great is the work?

sanskrit: yān suparṇāś ca gṛdhrāś ca vikarṣanti tatas tataḥ teṣāṃ tu karmaṇā lokā bhaviṣyanti yudhiṣṭhira
english: Those whom the great birds and the vultures drag this way and that — even for them, by their own deeds, the worlds shall be won, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam ukto mahāprājñaḥ kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ ādideśa sudharmāṇaṃ dhaumyaṃ sūtaṃ ca saṃjayam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed, the deeply wise Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Kuntī, gave command to Sudharman, to Dhaumya, to the charioteer Saṃjaya,

sanskrit: viduraṃ ca mahābuddhiṃ yuyutsuṃ caiva kauravam indrasenamukhāṃś caiva bhṛtyān sūtāṃś ca sarvaśaḥ
english: and to Vidura of great wisdom, and to Yuyutsu the Kaurava, and to the servants and charioteers headed by Indrasena, all of them together:

sanskrit: bhavantaḥ kārayantv eṣāṃ pretakāryāṇi sarvaśaḥ yathā cānāthavat kiṃ cic charīraṃ na vinaśyati
english: Let your honors have the funeral rites of these performed in full, so that no body shall perish unattended, as though it had no kin.

sanskrit: śāsanād dharmarājasya kṣattā sūtaś ca saṃjayaḥ sudharmā dhaumyasahita indrasenādayas tathā
english: At the command of the king of righteousness, the steward Vidura, the charioteer Saṃjaya, Sudharman together with Dhaumya, and Indrasena and the rest,

sanskrit: candanāgurukāṣṭhāni tathā kālīyakāny uta ghṛtaṃ tailaṃ ca gandhāṃś ca kṣaumāṇi vasanāni ca
english: gathering sandalwood and aloeswood and fragrant timber, clarified butter and oil and perfumes, and garments of fine linen,

sanskrit: samāhṛtya mahārhāṇi dārūṇāṃ caiva saṃcayān rathāṃś ca mṛditāṃs tatra nānāpraharaṇāni ca
english: and costly heaps of firewood, and the shattered chariots there, and weapons of every kind,

sanskrit: citāḥ kṛtvā prayatnena yathāmukhyān narādhipān dāhayām āsur avyagrā vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā
english: made the pyres with care and, calmly, by the rite prescribed in scripture, had the foremost of the kings cremated.

sanskrit: duryodhanaṃ ca rājānaṃ bhrātṝṃś cāsya śatādhikān śalyaṃ śalaṃ ca rājānaṃ bhūriśravasam eva ca
english: King Duryodhana and his brothers, more than a hundred of them, Śalya and King Śala, and Bhūriśravas as well,

sanskrit: jayadrathaṃ ca rājānam abhimanyuṃ ca bhārata dauḥśāsaniṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ ca dhṛṣṭaketuṃ ca pārthivam
english: and King Jayadratha and Abhimanyu, O Bhārata, the son of Duḥśāsana, and Lakṣmaṇa, and King Dhṛṣṭaketu,

sanskrit: bṛhantaṃ somadattaṃ ca sṛñjayāṃś ca śatādhikān rājānaṃ kṣemadhanvānaṃ virāṭadrupadau tathā
english: Bṛhanta and Somadatta and more than a hundred of the Sṛñjayas, King Kṣemadhanvan, and Virāṭa and Drupada too,

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍinaṃ ca pāñcālyaṃ dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ ca pārṣatam yudhāmanyuṃ ca vikrāntam uttamaujasam eva ca
english: Śikhaṇḍin the Pāñcāla and Dhṛṣṭadyumna son of Pṛṣata, and the valiant Yudhāmanyu and Uttamaujas as well,

sanskrit: kausalyaṃ draupadeyāṃś ca śakuniṃ cāpi saubalam acalaṃ vṛṣakaṃ caiva bhagadattaṃ ca pārthivam
english: the prince of Kosala and the sons of Draupadī, and Śakuni son of Subala, Acala and Vṛṣaka, and King Bhagadatta,

sanskrit: karṇaṃ vaikartanaṃ caiva sahaputram amarṣaṇam kekayāṃś ca maheṣvāsāṃs trigartāṃś ca mahārathān
english: and the wrathful Karṇa, son of the Sun, together with his sons, and the Kekayas, those mighty archers, and the Trigartas, those great chariot-warriors,

sanskrit: ghaṭotkacaṃ rākṣasendraṃ bakabhrātaram eva ca alambusaṃ ca rājānaṃ jalasaṃdhaṃ ca pārthivam
english: and Ghaṭotkaca, lord of the Rākṣasas, the brother of Baka, and King Alambusa, and King Jalasaṃdha,

sanskrit: anyāṃś ca pārthivān rājañ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ ghṛtadhārāhutair dīptaiḥ pāvakaiḥ samadāhayan
english: and other kings, O king, by the hundreds and the thousands — all these they had burned with blazing fires fed by streams of clarified butter.

sanskrit: pitṛmedhāś ca keṣāṃ cid avartanta mahātmanām sāmabhiś cāpy agāyanta te 'nvaśocyanta cāparaiḥ
english: For some of those great souls the rites for the fathers were performed; some were chanted over with hymns of the Sāman, and over others the mourners lamented.

sanskrit: sāmnām ṛcāṃ ca nādena strīṇāṃ ca ruditasvanaiḥ kaśmalaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ niśāyāṃ samapadyata
english: With the sound of the Sāman and the Ṛc verses, and the weeping cries of the women, a swooning faintness came upon all beings in the night.

sanskrit: te vidhūmāḥ pradīptāś ca dīpyamānāś ca pāvakāḥ nabhasīvānvadṛśyanta grahās tanvabhrasaṃvṛtāḥ
english: Those fires, smokeless, kindled and blazing, appeared as planets in the sky veiled by a thin haze of cloud.

sanskrit: ye cāpy anāthās tatrāsan nānādeśasamāgatāḥ tāṃś ca sarvān samānāyya rāśīn kṛtvā sahasraśaḥ
english: And those who were without kin there, come together from many lands — gathering them all and heaping them in piles by the thousands,

sanskrit: citvā dārubhir avyagraḥ prabhūtaiḥ snehatāpitaiḥ dāhayām āsa viduro dharmarājasya śāsanāt
english: Vidura, unhurried, having stacked them with abundant wood soaked in oil, had them burned at the command of the king of righteousness.

sanskrit: kārayitvā kriyās teṣāṃ kururājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ puraskṛtya gaṅgām abhimukho 'gamat
english: When he had had their rites performed, Yudhiṣṭhira, the king of the Kurus, set Dhṛtarāṣṭra before him and went toward the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca te samāsādya gaṅgāṃ tu śivāṃ puṇyajanocitām hradinīṃ vaprasaṃpannāṃ mahānūpāṃ mahāvanām
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: They came to the Gaṅgā, auspicious, frequented by holy folk, full of pools, rich in banks, with broad marshlands and great forests,

sanskrit: bhūṣaṇāny uttarīyāṇi veṣṭanāny avamucya ca tataḥ pitṝṇāṃ pautrāṇāṃ bhrātṝṇāṃ svajanasya ca
english: and casting off their ornaments, their upper garments, and their headcloths, then for their fathers, grandsons, brothers, and kindred,

sanskrit: putrāṇām āryakāṇāṃ ca patīnāṃ ca kurustriyaḥ udakaṃ cakrire sarvā rudantyo bhṛśaduḥkhitāḥ suhṛdāṃ cāpi dharmajñāḥ pracakruḥ salilakriyāḥ
english: for their sons and elders and husbands, all the women of the Kurus, weeping and sorely afflicted, made the water-offering; and the knowers of the law performed the libation rites for their friends as well.

sanskrit: udake kriyamāṇe tu vīrāṇāṃ vīrapatnibhiḥ sūpatīrthābhavad gaṅgā bhūyo viprasasāra ca
english: As the water-offering was made by the wives of the heroes for the heroes, the Gaṅgā came to have easy fords, and spread her waters wide again.

sanskrit: tan mahodadhisaṃkāśaṃ nirānandam anutsavam vīrapatnībhir ākīrṇaṃ gaṅgātīram aśobhata
english: That bank of the Gaṅgā, vast as the great ocean, joyless and without festival, thronged with the wives of the heroes, shone in its mournful splendor.

sanskrit: tataḥ kuntī mahārāja sahasā śokakarśitā rudatī mandayā vācā putrān vacanam abravīt
english: Then Kuntī, O great king, suddenly worn by grief, weeping, spoke to her sons in a faltering voice:

sanskrit: yaḥ sa śūro maheṣvāso rathayūthapayūthapaḥ arjunena hataḥ saṃkhye vīralakṣaṇalakṣitaḥ
english: That hero, the mighty archer, the leader of leaders of chariot-bands, who was slain in battle by Arjuna, marked with every sign of a hero —

sanskrit: yaṃ sūtaputraṃ manyadhvaṃ rādheyam iti pāṇḍavāḥ yo vyarājac camūmadhye divākara iva prabhuḥ
english: he whom you, O Pāṇḍavas, thought a charioteer's son, Rādheya — he who shone in the midst of the host like the radiant lord of day,

sanskrit: pratyayudhyata yaḥ sarvān purā vaḥ sapadānugān duryodhanabalaṃ sarvaṃ yaḥ prakarṣan vyarocata
english: who once fought against you all and your followers, who, leading on the whole army of Duryodhana, shone in his splendor,

sanskrit: yasya nāsti samo vīrye pṛthivyām api kaś cana satyasaṃdhasya śūrasya saṃgrāmeṣv apalāyinaḥ
english: to whose valor there is none equal on all the earth — true to his word, valiant, never fleeing in battle —

sanskrit: kurudhvam udakaṃ tasya bhrātur akliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ sa hi vaḥ pūrvajo bhrātā bhāskarān mayy ajāyata kuṇḍalī kavacī śūro divākarasamaprabhaḥ
english: make the water-offering for that brother of yours, untiring in his deeds. For he was your elder brother, born to me of the Sun, that hero with earrings and armor, whose splendor was like the maker of day.

sanskrit: śrutvā tu pāṇḍavāḥ sarve mātur vacanam apriyam karṇam evānuśocanta bhūyaś cārtatarābhavan
english: Hearing this unwelcome word of their mother, all the Pāṇḍavas grieved now for Karṇa, and became more stricken than before.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa puruṣavyāghraḥ kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ uvāca mātaraṃ vīro niḥśvasann iva pannagaḥ
english: Then that tiger among men, the heroic Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Kuntī, said to his mother, hissing like a serpent:

sanskrit: yasyeṣupātam āsādya nānyas tiṣṭhed dhanaṃjayāt kathaṃ putro bhavatyāṃ sa devagarbhaḥ purābhavat
english: He within whose arrow's flight none but Dhanaṃjaya could stand his ground — how was that god-begotten one of old a son of yours?
